- `wtf.term.free-energy.meaning`: Energy minus temperature times entropy; in Friston's free-energy principle, a bound on surprise an agent keeps low.
- `wtf.term.free-energy.usage`: SURPRISE is a game whose agent acts to keep its observations unsurprising, the free-energy principle in toy form.
- `wtf.term.gain.meaning`: The data input one clean stored pattern gives in a soft memory.
- `wtf.term.gain.usage`: The default is 64.
- `wtf.term.gibbs-sampling.meaning`: Re-tossing one variable at a time from its probability given all the others; for a p-bit that is the tanh rule.
- `wtf.term.gibbs-sampling.usage`: Named for Josiah Willard Gibbs. Glauber dynamics is the same rule in physics. settle-rs settles by Gibbs sampling.
- `wtf.term.gibbs-sweep.meaning`: One pass of Gibbs sampling over every free thing; settle records one sample per sweep.
- `wtf.term.gibbs-sweep.usage`: `settle 40_000` runs forty thousand sweeps after its burn-in. The hero's readout counts sweeps per second.
- `wtf.term.global-settle.meaning`: One registry of every settle on the page and one ripple that crosses them all: a ring of lights and a brief warming spreads from a click.
- `wtf.term.global-settle.usage`: settle-see's global.js. A ripple travels at 900 px a second and weakens with distance; each settle it crosses lights one crest and gets a small temperature kick. Nothing runs while no ripple travels, reduced motion shows one soft glow, and PAUSE ALL refuses it.
- `wtf.term.glossary.meaning`: This page and its system: every word on this site, what we mean by it, where it is used, and where it came from.
- `wtf.term.glossary.usage`: One record per term in src/wtf/terms.js. A harvest of the catalogue, the docs and the menu fails the tests when a word on the site has no record. Other parts read a word's meaning from here with termOf(id), and #/glossary# followed by a term's id opens that term. The old address #/wtf leads here.
- `wtf.term.gradient-descent.meaning`: Training by small steps against the gradient of a loss: θ ← θ − η∇L.
- `wtf.term.gradient-descent.usage`: A hero word, followed by its equation. The GRADSETTLE lane compared it with settling.
- `wtf.term.granule-cell.meaning`: In Kanerva's model of the cerebellum, a hard location: very many of them, each woken by a few mossy fibres.
- `wtf.term.granule-cell.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.grid.meaning`: Declares one thing per pixel of a picture.
- `wtf.term.grid.usage`: Written `grid :img, width: 64, height: 48`. The things are named img_x_y. The film player is a grid settling frame after frame.
- `wtf.term.hamiltonian-monte-carlo.meaning`: Sampling by giving the state a random momentum and following the energy's dynamics, which makes long moves that are rarely rejected.
- `wtf.term.hamiltonian-monte-carlo.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.hamming-ball.meaning`: Every address within a given Hamming distance of a centre; the Hamming distance counts the bits two words differ in.
- `wtf.term.hamming-ball.usage`: An address activates the hard locations inside its Hamming ball of the activation radius. The hero and WHAT draw it as a dashed circle.
- `wtf.term.hamming-distance.meaning`: The number of bit positions in which two words differ.
- `wtf.term.hamming-distance.usage`: An SDM measures every distance this way: an address activates the hard locations within the activation radius of it, and two random long words sit about half their bits apart.
- `wtf.term.hard-location.meaning`: One of the memory locations that is actually built, each with a fixed random address.
- `wtf.term.hard-location.usage`: Kanerva: "the hard locations are so few compared to the number of possible addresses." The keyword `hard-locations:` sets how many (it was `locations:`). A plain location is any point of the address space; a hard location is one that is built.
- `wtf.term.heat-bath.meaning`: The surroundings that hold a system at a fixed temperature T by exchanging energy with it.
- `wtf.term.heat-bath.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.hebbian.meaning`: A weight grows with the product of the activity at its two ends: cells that fire together wire together.
- `wtf.term.hebbian.usage`: A hero word, followed by the Hebbian rule a Hopfield memory stores its patterns with.
- `wtf.term.hero-strip.meaning`: The hero folded small: a 25 px still strip on other pages, or a 100 px live bar once pinned or scrolled away; the footer has a 50 px strip of its own.
- `wtf.term.hero-strip.usage`: A click on the hero's strip pins it for the visit and shows the live bar. The footer's strip is docked at the bottom until you reach the end of the page.
- `wtf.term.hero.meaning`: The big live picture at the top of the home page: p-bits settling into words, shapes and films about thermodynamic computing.
- `wtf.term.hero.usage`: Mounted once above the router, so it never restarts. On the home page it is full; scrolled away it becomes a 100 px live bar; on other pages it is a 25 px still strip until pinned. Its rotation is a random bag that never repeats an item twice in a row.
- `wtf.term.heteroassociative.meaning`: A memory that stores a word at another word's address: a pairing, or the next step of a sequence.
- `wtf.term.heteroassociative.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.hold.meaning`: Pins a thing to :yes or :no for the rest of the run block: what was seen.
- `wtf.term.hold.usage`: Written `hold :wet_grass, :yes` in a run block. Settle and anneal leave held things alone, so asking about the others answers a question with evidence. On the site held things are ice.
- `wtf.term.holographic-reduced-representation.meaning`: Plate's vector symbolic architecture: real-valued vectors bound by circular convolution.
- `wtf.term.holographic-reduced-representation.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.hopfield-memory.meaning`: A memory stored in the pulls: each pattern makes a valley, and settling from a damaged pattern falls back into it.
- `wtf.term.hopfield-memory.usage`: Named for John Hopfield. The memory family is a Hopfield memory, and the SDMMEMORY page recalls patterns live. Unlike an SDM it brings back mirror images.
- `wtf.term.hypercube.meaning`: The space of all n-bit words: each word is a corner, and the Hamming distance counts the edges between corners.
- `wtf.term.hypercube.usage`: An SDM's addresses are corners of a hypercube of thousands of dimensions, where almost every pair of corners is about half the bits apart.
- `wtf.term.hyperdimensional-computing.meaning`: Computing with very long random words, about ten thousand bits, using binding, adding and permuting.
- `wtf.term.hyperdimensional-computing.usage`: Kanerva's 2009 paper. Random long words are almost always far apart, which is what lets an SDM and the dollar of Mexico work.
- `wtf.term.hypervector.meaning`: A random vector of thousands of bits; two random ones almost surely differ in about half their bits.
- `wtf.term.hypervector.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.importance-sampling.meaning`: Averaging under p using samples drawn from q, each weighted by p/q.
- `wtf.term.importance-sampling.usage`: A hero word, followed by its equation.
- `wtf.term.inverse-temperature.meaning`: β = 1/T: how sharply the Boltzmann weights favour low energy.
- `wtf.term.inverse-temperature.usage`: A hero word. The hero's readout prints beta beside T.
- `wtf.term.ising-machine.meaning`: Hardware built to search for the lowest energy of an Ising model.
- `wtf.term.ising-machine.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.ising.meaning`: The Ising model: spins of +1 or -1 with fields and couplings, whose energy is exactly a SETTLE machine's.
- `wtf.term.ising.usage`: A thing is a spin, a lean is a field, a pull is a coupling. export writes a model in Ising form. ISTED after Ising is the hero's one joke.
- `wtf.term.isted.meaning`: The hero word after Ising, a rider's name: the hero's one joke.
- `wtf.term.isted.usage`: After the Ising item, half of the time, the caption reads ISTED? and a short film of a mountain-bike rider plays; a production build plays a rider drawn in code instead. The name lives in one constant, in src/heroFilms.js.
- `wtf.term.item-memory.meaning`: The store of named random hypervectors that a clean-up compares a noisy answer with.
- `wtf.term.item-memory.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.iterated-reads.meaning`: Reading again at the last answer: the most times a read uses its own result as the next read-address.
- `wtf.term.iterated-reads.usage`: Kanerva: "Such recovery typically takes several iterations (fewer than ten)" (2009, p. 144). A read stops early when its answer stops changing. The keyword was `iterations:`.
- `wtf.term.itunes-bloom.meaning`: Three soft blooms, low, middle and high, orbiting and swelling with their part of the sound.
- `wtf.term.itunes-bloom.usage`: One of the hero's eight visualisers, drawn from THE DJ's sound and shown in the slot the VISUALISERS bag holds.
- `wtf.term.jarzynski.meaning`: ⟨e^(−W/kT)⟩ = e^(−ΔF/kT): a free energy difference read from the work of many fast, non-equilibrium pulls.
- `wtf.term.jarzynski.usage`: A hero word, followed by its equation.
- `wtf.term.jax.meaning`: The Python library thrml is written in: thrml, Extropic's block Gibbs sampler, is a library in JAX.
- `wtf.term.jax.usage`: SETTLEBACKENDS cross-checked SETTLE against thrml 0.1.4 with jax and jaxlib 0.11.2; CREDITS lists it among the cross-checks.
- `wtf.term.jev.meaning`: In this project, a small head that predicts which experts a large model will route to next, trained on that model's own routing traces.
- `wtf.term.jev.usage`: It lets the engine fetch the experts before the model asks. SDMJEV does the same thing to SDMCHAT.
- `wtf.term.kanerva-package.meaning`: A Rust library that stores binary patterns in Kanerva's sparse distributed memory and reads them back from noisy read-addresses.
- `wtf.term.kanerva-package.usage`: KANERVA is the second package. Its README calls it Redis for sparse distributed memory. It has no dependencies, uses Kanerva's own words for every part, and the SETTLE interpreter depends on it by path. Its page is #/kanerva, in the packages folder of the menu, in electric cyan.
- `wtf.term.kanji-mark.meaning`: The brand mark: the kanji 定 (settle, fix) drawn as a dot matrix of lights in the prime red with a touch of neon.
- `wtf.term.kanji-mark.usage`: One source, BRAND_KANJI in src/brand.js, for the header, the favicon and the candidates on #/style. It settles in on the first paint.
- `wtf.term.key-legend.meaning`: The colour key in a page's corner, listing only the neons that page uses.
- `wtf.term.key-legend.usage`: Each page declares its neons in PAGE_NEONS in src/neon.js.
- `wtf.term.key.meaning`: Stores or reads text under a key: SETTLE's keyed notes.
- `wtf.term.key.usage`: With `key: "secret"` a write stores text that only the same key reads back; the read starts from the key's read-address.
- `wtf.term.kl-divergence.meaning`: D(p‖q) = Σ p ln(p/q): what coding p with a code built for q costs over the right code. It is never negative.
- `wtf.term.kl-divergence.usage`: A hero word, followed by its equation.
- `wtf.term.landauer.meaning`: Landauer's principle: erasing one bit costs at least kT ln 2 of heat.
- `wtf.term.landauer.usage`: Named for Rolf Landauer. It is why thermodynamic computing tries to use noise rather than fight it. One of the hero's words.
- `wtf.term.lane-boltzlearn.meaning`: The campaign lane whose question was: Can a settled machine learn a small classification task, against a plain baseline?
- `wtf.term.lane-boltzlearn.usage`: Its answer, as recorded: Yes: a machine with 64 hidden things reaches 93.8% on binarised digits against logistic regression at 91.2; shuffled labels give chance. Its scoreboard and tables are on RESULTS.
- `wtf.term.lane-doomworld.meaning`: The lane that turned the SURPRISE game into a textured, neon, multi-room world.
- `wtf.term.lane-doomworld.usage`: It built the level (seeded rooms, corridors and sliding doors) and the renderer. Its three spikers survive as the CLASSIC roster, the comparison the newer enemies are measured against.
- `wtf.term.lane-filmsharp.meaning`: The campaign lane whose question was: Can leans fitted to the grid itself hold the picture where TAP collapses, does a Rao-Blackwellised read recover the last 1 dB, and does another update rule mix faster?
- `wtf.term.lane-filmsharp.usage`: Its answer, as recorded: Fitted leans hold the horse to J 0.44, where TAP falls below 15 dB between 0.38 and 0.40. The rb read is the soft read in checkerboard order. Checkerboard Metropolised Gibbs lifts bits 80 at J 0.2 from 26.71 to 29.68 dB and the rb read from 35.44 to 39.88. Its scoreboard and tables are on RESULTS.
- `wtf.term.lane-gradsettle.meaning`: The campaign lane whose question was: Is gradient descent Settling, and what does the cloud of a hot fit give that one fitted model does not?
- `wtf.term.lane-gradsettle.usage`: Its answer, as recorded: T = 0 is gradient descent and T = 1 samples the posterior, checked exactly. On MNIST the T 1 posterior is less accurate than SGD; cooled it matches SGD, and four walkers give a doubt that finds rotated digits better than any single model. Its scoreboard and tables are on RESULTS.
- `wtf.term.lane-gridplayer.meaning`: The campaign lane whose question was: Does SETTLE reproduce the Python horse-player numbers, and how fast in Rust?
- `wtf.term.lane-gridplayer.usage`: Its answer, as recorded: p-bits play the horse but trail the Python player past 10 sweeps; pulls above 0.25 flip the grid to its mirror image. Its scoreboard and tables are on RESULTS.
- `wtf.term.lane-headclimb.meaning`: The Spark programme that runs beside the SETTLE campaign: beat the champion expert-prefetch head on its ruler, with the Spark fitting and recording.
- `wtf.term.lane-headclimb.usage`: SDMCHAT's plan says stage S1 could run on the Spark, at 20 tokens per parameter in about 3 days, after the HEADCLIMB lane ends; none of those stages has been run.
- `wtf.term.lane-perfladder.meaning`: The lane that profiled the site's live settles and made the engine faster: five quality levels, one picked at page load and kept for the visit, and the halt rule.
- `wtf.term.lane-perfladder.usage`: Every settle halts when the tab is hidden, or after 5 minutes with no input in the tab, and resumes when the tab is shown again or on any input. ?tier=1 to 5 picks a level by hand. The SURPRISE game's clock is settle-see's TRUE TIME from this lane.
- `wtf.term.lane-sdmchats.meaning`: The lane that put every SDM chat surface (SDMCHAT, SDMPOEM, SDMJEV, WEIRD LITTLE SDM GUY) on models that read an SDM, trained the wide-address SDM read at width 512 on the Spark, and added the loop guards to the sampler.
- `wtf.term.lane-sdmchats.usage`: Its measured loop check found the wide models looping on most chat replies with the old sampling settings and on none with the new ones.
- `wtf.term.lane-sdmcoded.meaning`: The campaign lane whose question was: Does compressing a note before storing it let more text fit and come back exactly, and is an error-correcting code worth its space?
- `wtf.term.lane-sdmcoded.usage`: Its answer, as recorded: Compression always helps: recovered text roughly doubles in every cell. An error-correcting code helps only against stray bits (crowded Hopfield, rate 0.75). The check turns every failure into a refusal: 0 silent wrong texts in 96,000 recalls. Its scoreboard and tables are on RESULTS.
- `wtf.term.lane-sdmexplore.meaning`: The lane that built the SDM state machine of the SDM EXPLORE page: a JavaScript port of settle-rs's sdm family.
- `wtf.term.lane-sdmexplore.usage`: It sealed nine checks of the page machine (X1 to X9) before measuring, among them that the JavaScript machine prints every read line of a SETTLE program byte for byte as the release binary; the results are in the campaign ledger.
- `wtf.term.lane-sdmkeys.meaning`: The campaign lane whose question was: Kanerva SDM against Hopfield capacity, fake valleys, fade, and what a key costs and protects.
- `wtf.term.lane-sdmkeys.usage`: Its answer, as recorded: SDM with 2000 locations beats Hopfield at 10-20% damage via the pulls read, loses at a matched pull count; no mirror images; a key protects the text but not the note's existence. Not cryptography. Its scoreboard and tables are on RESULTS.
- `wtf.term.lane-sdmkit.meaning`: The lane that lifted SETTLE's SDM code into KANERVA, a standalone Rust crate with no dependencies.
- `wtf.term.lane-sdmkit.usage`: settle-rs depends on KANERVA by path and its seven SDM files re-export it, so there is one implementation; the lane kept every output identical.
- `wtf.term.lane-sdmradius.meaning`: The campaign lane whose question was: If the SDM's radius is chosen for the damage it must survive, does 30% capacity grow with the number of locations, and does a pulls read scaled to the store's density work?
- `wtf.term.lane-sdmradius.usage`: Its answer, as recorded: Yes at 30%: P90 grows from 10 to 300 as M goes from 10,000 to 1,000,000. No at 40%: P90 stays at 1 to 3 at every M and radius, because a few whole patterns race for the read and the one sharing the most locations wins. The sealed density read failed; waking the top k rows worked and beats Hopfield at equal memory. Its scoreboard and tables are on RESULTS.
- `wtf.term.lane-sdmrefuse.meaning`: The lane that built a refusal rule for the SDM's top-k and wide-radius reads, from the race margin.
- `wtf.term.lane-sdmrefuse.usage`: Owed by SDMRADIUS; its statements are the sdmrefuse family. The WHAT page points to what it measured: how often each case is told apart.
- `wtf.term.lane-settlebackends.meaning`: The campaign lane whose question was: Emit a SETTLE model to other samplers' formats and cross-check: do thrml, dwave-samplers and exact enumeration agree?
- `wtf.term.lane-settlebackends.usage`: Its answer, as recorded: export/import in six forms; thrml 0.1.4 (Extropic), dwave-samplers 1.8.0 and exact enumeration agree with SETTLE on every sealed model; a flipped pull sign is caught. Its scoreboard and tables are on RESULTS.
- `wtf.term.lane-settlezoo.meaning`: The campaign lane whose question was: How often does annealing find the exact answer to a hard puzzle, against sweeps and size?
- `wtf.term.lane-settlezoo.usage`: Its answer, as recorded: Annealing finds exact answers where random guessing finds none: every sudoku, every colouring, max-cut from 16 nodes. Small factoring is a weak demonstration. Its scoreboard and tables are on RESULTS.
- `wtf.term.lane-smoothnumbers.meaning`: The campaign lane whose question was: Does settling solve linear systems, and how does the error fall with settling time?
- `wtf.term.lane-smoothnumbers.usage`: Its answer, as recorded: Noisy springs solve A x = b to 0.4-0.8% at t = 100,000; plain relaxation is about 1e8 times more accurate, so the noise pays only for the inverse. Its scoreboard and tables are on RESULTS.
- `wtf.term.lane-spark24.meaning`: The lane that ran the Spark GB10 as a priority job queue and trained SDMCHAT's newer models on it, on 300M tokens of FineWeb-Edu and the same held-out windows as SDMLLMSTORE.
- `wtf.term.lane-spark24.usage`: Its wide 512 model, which reads no SDM, holds the best TEST score of the SDMCHAT family, 1.42977 bits per byte, and is reported with its results; the chat offers only models that read an SDM. On 300M tokens the SDM read, the per-token table and no store at all tie (1.50641, 1.50680, 1.50670).
- `wtf.term.lane-valleymap.meaning`: The campaign lane whose question was: How many valleys does a settle landscape have, how wide, how regular, and what is the shape good for?
- `wtf.term.lane-valleymap.usage`: Its answer, as recorded: Valley count grows about e^(0.21 n); a seed plus a valley index needs about n bits to name an n-bit file (pigeonhole, measured); the landscape is useful as a prior, and not as a store. Its scoreboard and tables are on RESULTS.
- `wtf.term.lane-weirdguy.meaning`: The lane that made WEIRD LITTLE SDM GUY: SDMCHAT's SDM-read model fine-tuned on a corpus of our own.
- `wtf.term.lane-weirdguy.usage`: The fine-tune ran on the Spark, with the loss on the guy's turns only. His tiny paper on #/weirdlittlesdmguy names the lane and takes its numbers from the lane's report.
- `wtf.term.lane-zoohard.meaning`: The campaign lane whose question was: How does annealing fare on hard sudoku, on graph colouring near the threshold, and on factoring written column by column with carries?
- `wtf.term.lane-zoohard.usage`: Its answer, as recorded: On sudoku, the number of givens decides whether annealing succeeds, and the solving technique a puzzle needs does not. Colouring gets hard near the threshold (16% and 0% at n 160, degree 4.4 and 4.6). The column encoding factors up to 2,572,807 at one million sweeps where Rosenberg stops at 323, but its successes come from the best-so-far record of a walk that passes through the answer, and not from the state where the walk ends. Its scoreboard and tables are on RESULTS.
- `wtf.term.langevin.meaning`: Moving real numbers downhill on their energy plus a little noise set by the temperature.
- `wtf.term.langevin.usage`: The numbers and descend families use it; the cloud it draws is the answer and its spread.
- `wtf.term.ldpc.meaning`: An LDPC error-correcting code as springs: transmit through a noisy channel, then decode by settling or by belief propagation.
- `wtf.term.ldpc.usage`: decode_moves uses multi-bit moves; decode_nishimori settles at the Nishimori temperature.
- `wtf.term.lean-from.meaning`: Sets every pixel's lean from a picture file.
- `wtf.term.lean-from.usage`: Written `img.lean_from "frame.pgm"`. Dark pixels lean one way, light ones the other, so settling draws the picture in lights.
- `wtf.term.lean.meaning`: How much one thing wants to be yes on its own, before any pull: its field.
- `wtf.term.lean.usage`: Given with `leans: :yes, by: 1` (or :no) on `thing`. A positive lean pushes a thing toward yes. In physics a lean is the field h; on the site it is amber. A coin with lean 1 at temperature 1 comes up yes (1 + tanh 1) / 2 = 88.08% of the time.
- `wtf.term.learn.meaning`: Fits the leans and pulls to an example set: Boltzmann machine learning.
- `wtf.term.learn.usage`: Each round compares how often pairs agree in the examples and in the machine's own settles, and moves the pulls toward the examples.
- `wtf.term.level.meaning`: The largest allowed chance that a read accepts a read-address that was never stored.
- `wtf.term.level.usage`: Written alpha in the docs; the default is 0.01.
- `wtf.term.light.meaning`: A p-bit drawn as a dot of light: lit for yes, dim for no.
- `wtf.term.light.usage`: Every live picture on the site is lights settling. Their colours follow THE NEON CODE.
- `wtf.term.load-chip.meaning`: The header's load instrument: a small gauge of how much of the main thread the settles take, with a panel of the numbers; PAUSE ALL stops every live drawing, and it then reads HELD.
- `wtf.term.load-chip.usage`: In the header on every page. It turns amber with a dashed ring above 25% of the main thread (HIGH LOAD) and reads once every 500 ms, never while the tab is hidden. Its panel lists load, heap, settles, picture level and frames a second.
- `wtf.term.load.meaning`: How many random patterns the memory holds, for the refusal and recall predictions.
- `wtf.term.load.usage`: Written T in the docs.
- `wtf.term.logits.meaning`: The raw scores a network outputs before the softmax turns them into probabilities.
- `wtf.term.logits.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.magnetic-tunnel-junction.meaning`: Two magnetic layers around a thin insulator; made unstable on purpose, its resistance flips at random and it serves as one physical p-bit.
- `wtf.term.magnetic-tunnel-junction.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.magnetisation.meaning`: The average spin of a lattice: how ordered it is.
- `wtf.term.magnetisation.usage`: A hero word, followed by its equation.
- `wtf.term.majority-rule.meaning`: Bundling's last step: each bit takes the value most of the summed vectors hold.
- `wtf.term.majority-rule.usage`: A hero word, followed by its equation.
- `wtf.term.markov-blanket.meaning`: The things a thing depends on directly; given them, it is independent of everything else.
- `wtf.term.markov-blanket.usage`: In a SETTLE machine a thing's blanket is the things it pulls with, which is why each toss needs only its neighbours. SURPRISE uses the idea for an agent and its world.
- `wtf.term.master-beat.meaning`: One clock for the whole site: TRUE TIME ticks of 500 ms, a 120 bpm beat, a 2 s bar and the 25 ms flash of the 40 Hz light, all counted from one origin.
- `wtf.term.master-beat.usage`: settle-see's masterbeat.js holds it and settle-hear maps it onto the audio clock, so films, morphs, the hero's slots, the footer clock, the ripple, THE DJ's bars, the binaural pair and the 40 Hz light all start on shared ticks. A bar line is a tick, and a tick is a 40 Hz onset.
- `wtf.term.maxwells-demon.meaning`: Maxwell's imagined sorter of fast and slow molecules; erasing the demon's memory costs at least the entropy it saved, as Landauer's principle requires.
- `wtf.term.maxwells-demon.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.mcp-sdk.meaning`: The Model Context Protocol SDK: one of settle-mcp's two dependencies, the other being zod.
- `wtf.term.mcp-sdk.usage`: settle-mcp pins @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.31.0. The MCP page's recorded session was made by the official SDK client.
- `wtf.term.mean-field.meaning`: An approximation that replaces each neighbour by its average and solves one unit at a time.
- `wtf.term.mean-field.usage`: A hero word. TAP improves on it.
- `wtf.term.media-player-bars.meaning`: Thin bars standing on a floor, their reflection fading below it.
- `wtf.term.media-player-bars.usage`: One of the hero's eight visualisers, drawn from THE DJ's sound and shown in the slot the VISUALISERS bag holds.
- `wtf.term.memory-stmt.meaning`: Declares a Hopfield memory of `size` things.
- `wtf.term.memory-stmt.usage`: Written `memory :m, size: 64` in a model block. Its patterns live in the pulls between its things.
- `wtf.term.metropolis.meaning`: A sampling rule that proposes a flip and accepts it with probability min(1, e^(-ΔE/T)).
- `wtf.term.metropolis.usage`: A sibling of Gibbs sampling. The hero draws a Metropolis hop as one of its shapes.
- `wtf.term.midi.meaning`: A file format for notes: which pitch starts and stops when, on which channel, at what velocity, with a tempo and a meter. General MIDI fixes channel 10 as the drums and names each drum by a note number.
- `wtf.term.midi.usage`: THE BASES are built from open MIDI files (the Groove MIDI Dataset, Mutopia, OpenGameArt) by an importer that splits the notes by instrument and role, quantises them to a grid and records the error; the raw file never ships and the ledger keeps its licence and sha256.
- `wtf.term.milkdrop-field.meaning`: The last picture zoomed and turned, the wave drawn on top as a ring: the bass zooms, the treble turns.
- `wtf.term.milkdrop-field.usage`: One of the hero's eight visualisers, drawn from THE DJ's sound and shown in the slot the VISUALISERS bag holds.
- `wtf.term.mirror-image.meaning`: A stored pattern with every pixel reversed. The pulls record only which pixels agree with which, so it is a valley as well: E(-s) = E(s).
- `wtf.term.mirror-image.usage`: A Hopfield settle begun from noise often ends in a mirror. GRIDPLAYER found that pulls above 0.25 flip the whole grid to its mirror image; an SDM brings back no mirror images.
- `wtf.term.mixing-time.meaning`: How long a sampler must run before its samples no longer depend on where it started.
- `wtf.term.mixing-time.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.mixture-of-experts.meaning`: A layer of many expert networks with a router that sends each token to only a few of them, so most weights rest on any one token.
- `wtf.term.mixture-of-experts.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.mnist.meaning`: A standard set of handwritten digits, 28 by 28 pixels, used to test a learning machine.
- `wtf.term.mnist.usage`: The LEARNING page reads MNIST digits live with a settling machine, then shows the recorded lanes.
- `wtf.term.mode.meaning`: A soft read's mode: a one-way pass, or a joint settle with feedback.
- `wtf.term.mode.usage`: `mode: :pass` is the default.
- `wtf.term.model-block.meaning`: The block that declares a machine: its things, leans, pulls and any larger structure such as a grid or a memory.
- `wtf.term.model-block.usage`: Opened with `model :name do` and closed with `end`. Opening the same name again adds to the same model. Blocks cannot nest.
- `wtf.term.monte-carlo.meaning`: Estimating a sum or an average by drawing random samples.
- `wtf.term.monte-carlo.usage`: A hero word. ask counts samples in exactly this way.
- `wtf.term.mossy-fibre.meaning`: In Kanerva's model of the cerebellum, the input lines that carry the address.
- `wtf.term.mossy-fibre.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.mute-all.meaning`: The header button that silences every sound on the site; no other control can unmute it.
- `wtf.term.mute-all.usage`: Sound only starts after a click or a key, and MUTE ALL wins over all of it.
- `wtf.term.nearest-neighbour.meaning`: The stored word closest to a given one; an SDM read finds it approximately.
- `wtf.term.nearest-neighbour.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.neon-code.meaning`: Ten neons, each meaning one thing in every picture: yes rose, no indigo, lean amber, pull cyan, heat orange, calm lime, memory violet, held ice, data mint, miss red.
- `wtf.term.neon-code.usage`: One file, src/neon.js, feeds the stylesheet, the charts, the drawings and the KEY. The chrome around the pictures stays red light.
- `wtf.term.nishimori-temperature.meaning`: The temperature at which settling a decoder gives the best bit-by-bit guess for a given channel noise.
- `wtf.term.nishimori-temperature.usage`: c.decode_nishimori settles at it.
- `wtf.term.noise-contrastive-estimation.meaning`: Learning a density by learning to tell data from samples of a known noise distribution.
- `wtf.term.noise-contrastive-estimation.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.nonogram.meaning`: A picture puzzle whose rows and columns give run lengths; as leans and pulls, the hidden picture appears as it settles.
- `wtf.term.nonogram.usage`: The PUZZLES page settles nonograms live, in the same encoding as the zoo's puzzles: one start per block, blocks in order with a gap, cells that agree with both clues. The verdict is always the plain-code check of every row and column, never the energy.
- `wtf.term.number.meaning`: Declares a real-valued thing, a number, for the springs family.
- `wtf.term.number.usage`: Numbers sit on springs instead of being yes or no.
- `wtf.term.p-bit.meaning`: A probabilistic bit: a coin that comes up +1 or -1, biased by its input through the tanh rule.
- `wtf.term.p-bit.usage`: Every thing in a settle is a p-bit. Hardware p-bits exist as tiny magnets and transistors; on this site every p-bit is drawn as a light.
- `wtf.term.packages.meaning`: The three package pages, SETTLE, KANERVA and MCP: the main destinations, each in its own neon, first in every menu.
- `wtf.term.packages.usage`: The menu groups them in the packages folder. Each wears a small [pkg] tag and its own colour: bright purple for SETTLE, electric cyan for KANERVA, acid chartreuse for MCP. A package page opens with the repository top: the kicker, the quotes, the install panel. A new package adds one row to PACKAGE_NEONS in src/neon.js.
- `wtf.term.page-ask.meaning`: One page where a member asks what SETTLE and KANERVA are, answered by a language model reading the site's own docs.
- `wtf.term.page-ask.usage`: In the account folder. Ten free questions a member; after that the page says more questions use credits. The only thing on the site that uses credits.
- `wtf.term.page-contact.meaning`: How to reach us: an address to copy, the X handle, the repository note and one line in the site's voice.
- `wtf.term.page-contact.usage`: In the about folder. The address and the handle read "not set yet" until the navigator fills two constants in src/contact.js.
- `wtf.term.page-credits.meaning`: Who and what SETTLE rests on, Pentti Kanerva first, every citation checked against its link.
- `wtf.term.page-credits.usage`: In the about folder.
- `wtf.term.page-film.meaning`: A grid of p-bits playing film frames live, every stage shown: target, leans, lights, bits and the error map.
- `wtf.term.page-film.usage`: The Muybridge horse and Tears of Steel, each frame drawn by settling from the last.
- `wtf.term.page-hear.meaning`: settle-hear on the site: a mixing desk on one live settle, the demo setups, and what each sound means.
- `wtf.term.page-hear.usage`: In the language folder.
- `wtf.term.page-home.meaning`: The home page: the hero, GETTING STARTED, the statement families and the campaign summary.
- `wtf.term.page-home.usage`: Its path in the menu is /settle itself. It shows a four-line program running live under its code.
- `wtf.term.page-learning.meaning`: A settling machine that reads handwritten digits: MNIST live, then the 8x8 lanes as recorded.
- `wtf.term.page-learning.usage`: Boltzmann machine learning in the browser.
- `wtf.term.page-members.meaning`: Your account: sign up, log in, and the little guys and runs you saved from the studio, each to download or delete.
- `wtf.term.page-members.usage`: In the account folder. The saved models come first; the password, your data export and account deletion follow. Accounts need the site's small server, so a copy without it says so.
- `wtf.term.page-numbers.meaning`: Springs that solve A x = b live: the cloud's centre finds the answer, its spread gives the inverse.
- `wtf.term.page-numbers.usage`: The numbers family, drawn.
- `wtf.term.page-paper.meaning`: "On the Lime and the Coconut": SETTLE's whole mathematics as one very short paper.
- `wtf.term.page-paper.usage`: In the science folder.
- `wtf.term.page-puzzles.meaning`: Live annealing of sudoku, graph colouring, max-cut and factoring, then the recorded success rates.
- `wtf.term.page-puzzles.usage`: Each puzzle is leans and pulls; anneal looks for the calmest arrangement and a plain-code check judges it.
- `wtf.term.page-relax.meaning`: The cool-down class: Richard and DHH do aerobics in settles while it teaches how a machine settles.
- `wtf.term.page-relax.usage`: In the science folder.
- `wtf.term.page-results.meaning`: Every lane's scoreboard, headline numbers and tables; one lane's full report; the campaign ledger.
- `wtf.term.page-results.usage`: A lane is one named piece of work in the SETTLE campaign. Each wrote its predictions before measuring, then scored them HIT, SPLIT or MISS.
- `wtf.term.page-sdmexplore.meaning`: An SDM drawn as a state diagram you operate, how SDMCHAT works, and six SETTLE x KANERVA experiments.
- `wtf.term.page-sdmexplore.usage`: One idea per section: the machine, the address, the vote, the warm read, the program and what the binary printed.
- `wtf.term.page-sdmmemory.meaning`: Live Hopfield recall, an SDM room of lights, the softness dial and keyed notes, then the record.
- `wtf.term.page-sdmmemory.usage`: In the demos folder. The old address #/memory leads here.
- `wtf.term.page-sdmpoem.meaning`: The SDM language model writing verse live, then THE POEM LAB: an SDM that learns a whole poem in the tab and recites it.
- `wtf.term.page-sdmpoem.usage`: In the demos folder. The old address #/poem leads here.
- `wtf.term.page-surprise.meaning`: A first-person game whose settling agent acts to keep its surprise low: Friston's free-energy principle in toy form.
- `wtf.term.page-surprise.usage`: With the explanation, the measured runs and the sources.
- `wtf.term.page-valleys.meaning`: The shape of a settle landscape: a live exact valley map and a live grid survey.
- `wtf.term.page-valleys.usage`: The valleys family, drawn.
- `wtf.term.page-what.meaning`: What SETTLE is, step by step, in two halves: SETTLE, then KANERVA.
- `wtf.term.page-what.usage`: Each half opens with plain words (WAT DIS), how it works (HOW DAT), what it does (WAT DAT) and who it rests on (WHO DIS). #/what#sdm opens the KANERVA half.
- `wtf.term.page-who-you-are.meaning`: Three guides on one page, one per reader: a computer programmer (with machine learning and other problems), a visual artist, a sound artist. Each says what SETTLE, KANERVA and settle-mcp are in that reader's terms, how to use them in a project, one real example with its real output, a getting-started, and links into the detailed docs.
- `wtf.term.page-who-you-are.usage`: In the language folder beside WHAT, the tour's stop after it, and the home page's first link. The guides are Markdown files, one folder per reader under docs/who-you-are/, rendered by the package docs renderer; settle-mcp carries the same files as its first resources and writes its AGENTS.md from them.
- `wtf.term.parallel-tempering.meaning`: Copies of a system run at several temperatures and swap states now and then, so the cold copy escapes its traps.
- `wtf.term.parallel-tempering.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.partition-function.meaning`: Z, the sum of e^(−E/T) over every state: the number that turns Boltzmann weights into probabilities.
- `wtf.term.partition-function.usage`: A hero word, followed by its equation. Its log gives the free energy: F = −kT ln Z.
- `wtf.term.pentti-kanerva.meaning`: Pentti Kanerva, who invented sparse distributed memory and wrote the hyperdimensional computing papers this site leans on.
- `wtf.term.pentti-kanerva.usage`: His 1988 book and 1993 chapter name every part of the memory, and SETTLE takes his words. The CREDITS page uses the shapes of his memory as his portrait, because no photograph of him is freely licensed.
- `wtf.term.permutation.meaning`: Rotating or shuffling a hypervector's bits in a fixed way: the operation that marks order or position.
- `wtf.term.permutation.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.perplexity.meaning`: e raised to the cross-entropy: the number of equally likely choices a model is as unsure as.
- `wtf.term.perplexity.usage`: A hero word, followed by its equation.
- `wtf.term.pgm.meaning`: Plain picture files: PGM holds one grey value a pixel, PPM three colour values a pixel.
- `wtf.term.pgm.usage`: img.lean_from reads a binary PGM (P5) of exactly the grid's size, img.show_as writes one, and the colour family reads and writes PPM. The film player's frames are PGM files.
- `wtf.term.phase-transition.meaning`: A sharp change of order as the temperature crosses a critical point.
- `wtf.term.phase-transition.usage`: A hero word, followed by the magnet-flip film.
- `wtf.term.play.meaning`: Plays a folder of picture frames through a grid, settling each frame from the last.
- `wtf.term.play.usage`: Written `play :img, frames: "dir/"`. play_colour does the same with three grids, one per colour.
- `wtf.term.probabilistic-computer.meaning`: A machine built of p-bits that samples from a distribution instead of computing one answer.
- `wtf.term.probabilistic-computer.usage`: A hero word. SETTLE programs one in software.
- `wtf.term.psnr.meaning`: Peak signal-to-noise ratio, in dB, of a picture read from a settle.
- `wtf.term.psnr.usage`: THE PAPER shows that a picture read this way gains 3.01 dB at each doubling of K. The film lanes report the median PSNR over the horse's frames for each sweep budget.
- `wtf.term.pull.meaning`: A coupling between two things that makes them agree; a push is a negative pull that makes them disagree.
- `wtf.term.pull.usage`: Written `a.pulls :b, by: 2` or `a.pushes :b, by: 1` in a model block. Pulls are symmetric and add up. In physics a pull is the coupling J; on the site it is cyan.
- `wtf.term.purkinje-cell.meaning`: The large neuron of the cerebellar cortex; Marr and Albus read the cerebellum as a memory, and Kanerva saw an SDM in it.
- `wtf.term.purkinje-cell.usage`: The footer's brain draws a layer of cerebellar cortex with its fans of Purkinje cells; one hero film grows one.
- `wtf.term.quantum-annealing.meaning`: Annealing that crosses energy barriers by quantum tunnelling instead of by heat.
- `wtf.term.quantum-annealing.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.quasi-orthogonal.meaning`: Two random hypervectors are almost perpendicular: they differ in close to half their bits.
- `wtf.term.quasi-orthogonal.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.qubo.meaning`: A cost written as a quadratic in 0/1 variables; it turns into leans and pulls directly.
- `wtf.term.qubo.usage`: The puzzles are written as QUBOs and settled. export writes a model as QUBO.
- `wtf.term.random-address.meaning`: A hard location's address, drawn at random once and never changed.
- `wtf.term.random-address.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.rate-the-dj.meaning`: Five star glyphs among the hero's own text lines: the middle left of the full hero, the top left of its bar. A click rates the set THE DJ is playing.
- `wtf.term.rate-the-dj.usage`: A rating counts only after a humanity check on real pointer movement; before that it is held. Rating the same set again replaces the first rating. The ratings stay in this browser unless a feedback endpoint is set.
- `wtf.term.read-address.meaning`: The address you read a memory at.
- `wtf.term.read-address.usage`: Kanerva: "When x is used as the retrieval address, the locations activated by x are pooled" (1993, P. 6); he also says retrieval cue and memory cue. SETTLE says read because the statement is `m.read`. The keyword was `cue:`; a program that still writes `cue:` stops with an error naming `read-address:`.
- `wtf.term.read-threshold.meaning`: A read sums the bit-counters of the activated hard locations and keeps each bit whose sum is above 0.
- `wtf.term.read-threshold.usage`: Kanerva: "the sums are compared to a threshold value 0 to get an output vector z" (1993, P. 6). A sum of exactly 0 keeps the old bit.
- `wtf.term.read.meaning`: Reads a memory at a read-address: the activated hard locations vote, bit by bit, and the read repeats from its own answer.
- `wtf.term.read.usage`: Written `m.read read-address: :cat, address-noise: 0.2, iterated-reads: 10`.
- `wtf.term.recall.meaning`: Reads a pattern back from a Hopfield memory by settling from a noisy read-address.
- `wtf.term.recall.usage`: Written `m.recall read-address: :cat, address-noise: 0.2`. The machine settles into the nearest stored valley.
- `wtf.term.red-light-rule.meaning`: The site's chrome emits red light only, 600 nm and up, with a few named exceptions: the pinks, the purple highlight, the code purple, and the logo's own lights (its touch neons and its PLAIN WHITE moment).
- `wtf.term.red-light-rule.usage`: Headings are HYPER PINK, action buttons HOT PINK, SETTLE and KANERVA code bright purple, and pictures use THE NEON CODE.
- `wtf.term.refusal.meaning`: Computes when a memory read should refuse to answer: when the read-address was never stored.
- `wtf.term.refusal.usage`: It works exactly, without building a memory, from the load and the allowed false-accept level.
- `wtf.term.remember.meaning`: Stores a pattern (or a line of text) in a Hopfield memory's pulls.
- `wtf.term.remember.usage`: Written `m.remember :cat`. Each stored pattern deepens one valley of the memory's landscape.
- `wtf.term.replica.meaning`: A way to average ln Z over random pulls: compute the average of Z^n for n copies of the system, and let n go to 0.
- `wtf.term.replica.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.restricted-boltzmann-machine.meaning`: A Boltzmann machine with pulls only between a visible layer and a hidden layer, never within a layer.
- `wtf.term.restricted-boltzmann-machine.usage`: A hero word, followed by the Boltzmann machine picture.
- `wtf.term.role-filler-binding.meaning`: A role vector bound to a filler vector, so a bundled record can be taken apart again by unbinding.
- `wtf.term.role-filler-binding.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.rounds.meaning`: How many passes or reads a statement makes.
- `wtf.term.rounds.usage`: On softsdm, how many times each read is fed its own last result; on learn, passes over the rows.
- `wtf.term.run-block.meaning`: The block that runs a declared model: it holds things, settles, anneals, shows and asks.
- `wtf.term.run-block.usage`: Opened with `run :name do` for a model opened earlier in the file, and closed with `end`. Each run block starts at temperature 1 with its generator seeded 24301.
- `wtf.term.run-state.meaning`: What a run block remembers between its statements: the temperature, the random generator, the held things and the last samples.
- `wtf.term.run-state.usage`: A settle records samples into the run state, and show, best and ask read them back. The model's notes are where larger structures (a memory, a grid) keep their own state.
- `wtf.term.sample.meaning`: One recorded arrangement of the machine; counting samples estimates probabilities.
- `wtf.term.sample.usage`: A settle records one sample per sweep. Samples next to each other are correlated, so the docs explain how to read error bars from them.
- `wtf.term.samples.meaning`: How many samples each soft read takes.
- `wtf.term.samples.usage`: A soft read is noisy, so it averages several.
- `wtf.term.save-coded.meaning`: Compresses and error-codes text, then stores it; recall_coded reads it back and decodes it.
- `wtf.term.save-coded.usage`: The coding lets a memory hold more text and survive noise in what comes back.
- `wtf.term.save.meaning`: Stores text in a memory under a key, so it can be read back with the key.
- `wtf.term.save.usage`: Written `m.save "text", key: "secret"`.
- `wtf.term.score-matching.meaning`: Fitting the gradient of the log density (the score) instead of the density, so the partition function is never needed.
- `wtf.term.score-matching.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.sdm-stmt.meaning`: Declares a Kanerva sparse distributed memory: hard locations with random addresses and bit-counters.
- `wtf.term.sdm-stmt.usage`: Written `sdm :m, word-size: 256, hard-locations: 2000`. Nothing is written yet.
- `wtf.term.sdmchat.meaning`: An SDM used as a language model, running as a live chat in the browser.
- `wtf.term.sdmchat.usage`: It reads the context as a read-address and votes on the next token, at the DeepSeek V4 vocabulary. The page then shows the recorded SDMLLM and SDMLLMSTORE results. SDMJEV reads its vector space. The old addresses #/llm and #/chatsdm lead here.
- `wtf.term.sdmjev.meaning`: The model magic-8-ball: a yes, unsure or no decision read in one pass from SDMCHAT's vector space and settled into one of the twenty classic answers.
- `wtf.term.sdmjev.usage`: Each answer is taken apart on the page: the teacher's read, the student's lean and its cut-offs, the vector it read, the settle's run. The old address #/magic8 leads here.
- `wtf.term.sdmscale-stmt.meaning`: A sparse distributed memory at scale, up to a million hard locations, built on the KANERVA crate.
- `wtf.term.sdmscale-stmt.usage`: put adds a named pattern; fill adds unnamed patterns as load.
- `wtf.term.sdmstudio.meaning`: A little ML studio in the browser: post-train one of the site's SDM chat models on a licensed dataset or your own text, with loss curves, samples, checkpoints and a file tree of your runs.
- `wtf.term.sdmstudio.usage`: The WEIRD LITTLE SDM GUY page is its prime use; SDMCHAT and SDMPOEM mount the same panel. A run trains in a Web Worker for as long as you like up to a 7-day cap, a product rule; runs live in this browser and need no account. The old address #/studio leads here.
- `wtf.term.seed.meaning`: The keyword that replaces a run's random generator with one seeded by a number, so a run repeats exactly.
- `wtf.term.seed.usage`: Every run block starts seeded 24301. Most statements that draw at random take `seed:`; on an sdm it seeds the random addresses of the hard locations.
- `wtf.term.sequence-memory.meaning`: A sequence is stored by writing each word at the address of the one before it, so reading at one word recalls the next.
- `wtf.term.sequence-memory.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.settle-hear.meaning`: SETTLE's hearing library: it makes sound from a settle's own numbers.
- `wtf.term.settle-hear.usage`: A JavaScript library beside settle-see; settle-see never imports it. It holds the mixing desk on #/hear, the hero symphony, the binaural pair and MUTE ALL. Sound only starts after a click or a key, and MUTE ALL silences all of it.
- `wtf.term.settle-mcp.meaning`: settle-mcp, a Model Context Protocol server that lets an assistant read the SETTLE and KANERVA docs, set them up and run programs.
- `wtf.term.settle-mcp.usage`: The third package. It runs on stdio and has three parts: docs and help, setup, and tools that run SETTLE programs and Kanerva memories. Its docs are generated from this site, which is their source of truth. Its page is #/mcp, in acid chartreuse.
- `wtf.term.settle-see.meaning`: SETTLE's seeing library: every picture it draws is a grid of p-bits settling out of noise into a word or a shape.
- `wtf.term.settle-see.usage`: A JavaScript library with no dependencies, in experiments/thermosim/settle-see. The hero, the footer brain, the credits marks and most live drawings on this site are settle-see. It reports the settle's stats a few times a second, which settle-hear turns into sound.
- `wtf.term.settle-stmt.meaning`: The statement that settles a model: N Gibbs sweeps at a temperature, recording one sample per sweep.
- `wtf.term.settle-stmt.usage`: Written `settle 40_000, temperature: 1, seed: 1`. It starts every free thing at random, throws away a tenth as burn-in, then records. show and ask read those samples.
- `wtf.term.settle-text.meaning`: settle-text, the React component library: text, images and vectors rendered as a live settle of lights, with no theory needed.
- `wtf.term.settle-text.usage`: The fourth package. Four components, SettleText, SettleImage, SettleVector and SettleBackground, wrap settle-see and take plain props: the words and the font, a colour, a size, a resolution preset, a glow. Its defaults are this site's measured title tuning. Its page is #/settletext, in laser green.
- `wtf.term.settle.meaning`: A small programming language for settling machines: you declare things, leans and pulls, then let them settle and count.
- `wtf.term.settle.usage`: SETTLE names the language and its interpreter, settle-rs, a Rust program. A program has model blocks that declare the machine and run blocks that hold, settle and ask. On this site SETTLE is the first package page and the menu item that opens the docs. In running text the name stays in Latin letters; the hero draws it as セトル.
- `wtf.term.settling.meaning`: Sampling by re-tossing one thing at a time, so that every arrangement turns up with probability proportional to e^(-E/T).
- `wtf.term.settling.usage`: The process the machine runs and the language is named for. In the long run low-energy arrangements turn up most. The hero's phase word "settled" says the picture has reached its valley.
- `wtf.term.show-as.meaning`: Writes the grid as a picture file.
- `wtf.term.show-as.usage`: Written `img.show_as "out.pgm"`. With `from: :rate` each pixel's grey is how often it was yes.
- `wtf.term.show.meaning`: Prints one line per thing: how often it was yes in the last settle, with a bar.
- `wtf.term.show.usage`: Written `show` in a run block after a settle. It is the quickest look at what a settle found.
- `wtf.term.simulated-annealing.meaning`: Settling while slowly lowering the temperature, so the machine ends in a deep valley.
- `wtf.term.simulated-annealing.usage`: Named after the metalworking practice. anneal does it in SETTLE and the puzzles solve by it.
- `wtf.term.soft-read.meaning`: A picture drawn from each light's running average, rather than from its bits, which are fully on or off.
- `wtf.term.soft-read.usage`: The SURPRISE game can draw it, and the film lanes score it beside the bits: GRIDPLAYER's soft read capped near 29 dB. FILMSHARP's rb read is the soft read in checkerboard order.
- `wtf.term.softmax.meaning`: Turns scores into probabilities: e to each score over T, divided by the sum of them all. It is the Boltzmann distribution of the scores.
- `wtf.term.softmax.usage`: A hero word, an equation picture, and a live film where T sweeps and the five probabilities are computed as it moves.
- `wtf.term.softness.meaning`: How wide the soft edge of the activation radius is; 0 is hard SDM.
- `wtf.term.softness.usage`: Measured in units of sqrt(word size) / 2 bits. The SDMMEMORY page has a softness dial.
- `wtf.term.softsdm-stmt.meaning`: A sparse distributed memory built from p-bits: hard locations activate with a probability, not a sharp cut.
- `wtf.term.softsdm-stmt.usage`: attend runs three reads from one read-address. The softness keyword sets how wide the soft edge is; 0 is hard SDM.
- `wtf.term.solution.meaning`: Takes the best arrangement of the last anneal, decodes the puzzle from it and checks it in plain code.
- `wtf.term.solution.usage`: Written `x.solution`. anneal_each walks the same path as anneal and keeps more of it. The verdict is always the check, never the energy.
- `wtf.term.sonique-ring.meaning`: 32 rays all the way round, low notes at the top, the ring turning slowly.
- `wtf.term.sonique-ring.usage`: One of the hero's eight visualisers, drawn from THE DJ's sound and shown in the slot the VISUALISERS bag holds.
- `wtf.term.sound.meaning`: The hero's sound button: off on load, in the hot pink action style while off.
- `wtf.term.sound.usage`: Turning it on plays DEFAULT MODE unless another mix was picked.
- `wtf.term.sparse-coding.meaning`: Codes in which most bits are 0 and only a few are 1.
- `wtf.term.sparse-coding.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.sparse-distributed-memory.meaning`: Pentti Kanerva's memory: a word is written to many hard locations near its address and read back by their vote, even from a noisy address.
- `wtf.term.sparse-distributed-memory.usage`: An SDM has a few hard locations scattered in a huge space of addresses. A write adds the data word to the bit-counters of every hard location within the activation radius; a read sums those counters and keeps the sign. SETTLE has sdm, softsdm and sdmscale; KANERVA is the crate. SDMCHAT is an SDM used as a language model.
- `wtf.term.sparsity.meaning`: Most units silent at once, so each pattern uses only a few.
- `wtf.term.sparsity.usage`: A hero word. Kanerva's memory is sparse in the same sense: an address wakes a tiny share of the hard locations.
- `wtf.term.spike.meaning`: A pulse travelling along a wire in the footer's brain picture.
- `wtf.term.spike.usage`: Drawn on the brain bands as they settle.
- `wtf.term.spin-glass.meaning`: Spins coupled by random pulls of both signs: an energy landscape of countless valleys.
- `wtf.term.spin-glass.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.springs.meaning`: Ties numbers together with springs: springs pulls two together, opposes pulls one toward minus the other, leans_to ties one to a value.
- `wtf.term.springs.usage`: Each spring adds a quadratic energy; a set of springs is a linear system A x = b.
- `wtf.term.statement-family.meaning`: One Rust file of settle-rs that adds a group of statements, such as core, memory or sdm.
- `wtf.term.statement-family.usage`: The interpreter offers each line to the twenty families in a fixed order, and the first whose pattern matches runs it. The home page lists every family with its glyph.
- `wtf.term.stochastic-computing.meaning`: Computing on random bit streams in which the share of 1s carries the number; a gate that gives 1 only when both its inputs are 1 then multiplies two numbers.
- `wtf.term.stochastic-computing.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.stochastic-resonance.meaning`: A weak periodic signal made easier to detect by adding the right amount of noise.
- `wtf.term.stochastic-resonance.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.sudoku.meaning`: Turns a puzzle into leans and pulls: sudoku, graph colouring, max-cut and factoring.
- `wtf.term.sudoku.usage`: Each declares the things and pulls whose calmest arrangement is a solution; anneal finds one and x.solution checks it. The PUZZLES page runs them live.
- `wtf.term.superposition.meaning`: Many patterns stored on the same weights at once.
- `wtf.term.superposition.usage`: A hero word. A Hopfield memory and an SDM both store this way.
- `wtf.term.symbol.meaning`: A word with a colon in front, such as :rain; a thing's name and the values :yes and :no are symbols.
- `wtf.term.symbol.usage`: The lexer reads seven kinds of token: symbols (:rain), labels (by:), identifiers, numbers, strings, commas and dots. :yes and :no are the two values of a thing and cannot name one.
- `wtf.term.tanh-rule.meaning`: P(yes) = (1 + tanh(I / T)) / 2, where I is a thing's lean plus its pulls times its neighbours.
- `wtf.term.tanh-rule.usage`: The rule each toss follows. With lean 1 and no pulls at temperature 1, a thing is yes 88.08% of the time. The hero's softness film draws it beside a live field.
- `wtf.term.tap-correction.meaning`: A correction to the leans that aim at a picture: subtract what the neighbours already push, and add back the part of that push which is the pixel's own influence reflected by its neighbours.
- `wtf.term.tap-correction.usage`: The film player's leans are none, mean-field or TAP. GRIDPLAYER-2 found TAP leans beat mean-field on 20 of 20 exact targets; FILMSHARP found fitted leans hold the horse where TAP collapses.
- `wtf.term.temperature-kw.meaning`: The keyword that sets a run's temperature, for this statement and the ones after it.
- `wtf.term.temperature-kw.usage`: A run block starts at temperature 1. Hotter means more random tosses; colder means each thing follows its lean and pulls more closely.
- `wtf.term.temperature.meaning`: How random the tosses are; β = 1/T. Hot is noisy, cold follows the energy closely.
- `wtf.term.temperature.usage`: In physics the temperature enters as kT; SETTLE folds k into the units. On the site heat is orange.
- `wtf.term.the-dj.meaning`: The part of the hero symphony that picks the flute and old tunes from the picture, shown as one line at the bottom of the hero.
- `wtf.term.the-dj.usage`: settle-hear's symphony: a 432 Hz binaural pair on a 40 Hz beat, the flute and old tunes chosen by THE DJ. THE SPECTRUM interleaves live items while its house set is heard.
- `wtf.term.the-navigator.meaning`: The person who directs this work: he charts the course and makes the calls.
- `wtf.term.the-navigator.usage`: Rulings in the code and the docs are dated and attributed to the navigator.
- `wtf.term.thermodynamic-computing.meaning`: Computing with hardware that settles toward equilibrium, so that its own thermal noise does the sampling.
- `wtf.term.thermodynamic-computing.usage`: A hero word, and the subject of this whole site.
- `wtf.term.thermosim.meaning`: The folder the SETTLE campaign lives in, and its Python player: a simulated thermodynamic chip settling into video frames.
- `wtf.term.thermosim.usage`: THERMOSIM's Python player is the smooth analogue version of the film player's idea. Its median PSNR per budget on the Muybridge horse is the yardstick the Rust lanes were compared with.
- `wtf.term.thing.meaning`: A yes-or-no unit of a program; the statement `thing` declares one or more and can give them a lean.
- `wtf.term.thing.usage`: Written `thing :a, :b, leans: :yes, by: 1` in a model block. A thing is drawn on this site as a light, and in physics it is a spin. Leans add up across declarations.
- `wtf.term.tolerate-noise.meaning`: The address-noise a memory is sized to tolerate; SETTLE picks the activation radius that recalls best at that noise.
- `wtf.term.tolerate-noise.usage`: SETTLE's own keyword, built from Kanerva's word noise. It was `tolerate:` and overrides `activation-probability:`.
- `wtf.term.transformer.meaning`: A network of stacked attention layers and small feed-forward nets; the shape of today's large language models.
- `wtf.term.transformer.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.true-time.meaning`: A film keeps its own pace behind, and the field in front settles toward whatever frame is current, frame by frame.
- `wtf.term.true-time.usage`: settle-see's truetime.js. The film player, the hero films, the footer brain and the morphs all play in TRUE TIME, and it measures how many changed lights the field caught.
- `wtf.term.two-panels.meaning`: The two kinds of panel around a block of text. The purple panel holds SETTLE and KANERVA code and stays stock standard, because it stands for a standard library. The orange notation panel, a chamfered frame around a paragraph of our own notation, is ours.
- `wtf.term.two-panels.usage`: The two sentences on Settling on the home page wear the orange notation panel; every program block and install box wears the purple one.
- `wtf.term.uci-digits.meaning`: The small set of 8x8 handwritten digits bundled with scikit-learn.
- `wtf.term.uci-digits.usage`: BOLTZLEARN learned from these digits; the LEARNING page reads MNIST live and shows the 8x8 lanes as recorded.
- `wtf.term.unbinding.meaning`: XOR a bundled record with a role again, and a noisy copy of its filler comes back out.
- `wtf.term.unbinding.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.valleys-stmt.meaning`: Lists the calm arrangements of a small machine exactly; survey samples them in a larger one.
- `wtf.term.valleys-stmt.usage`: landscape builds a test landscape. The VALLEYS page draws the map live.
- `wtf.term.variational-inference.meaning`: Approximating a hard distribution with a simpler q chosen to lower a free energy, the negative ELBO.
- `wtf.term.variational-inference.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.vector-symbolic-architecture.meaning`: The family of algebras on wide vectors: a bind, a bundle and a permutation.
- `wtf.term.vector-symbolic-architecture.usage`: A hero word.
- `wtf.term.verdict.meaning`: The three verdicts on a prediction a lane wrote before it measured: right, partly right, wrong.
- `wtf.term.verdict.usage`: Every lane of the campaign sealed its predictions in the ledger first, then scored them. The home page totals them and each lane's page lists its misses with the rest.
- `wtf.term.via.meaning`: Which read an sdm runs: Kanerva's read by addresses, or a zero-temperature settle of the pulls.
- `wtf.term.via.usage`: `via: :addresses` is the default; `via: :pulls` reads the same memory as a SETTLE machine.
- `wtf.term.visualisers.meaning`: The hero's second bag: eight pictures of the sound, after the old music players, one slot in every eight.
- `wtf.term.visualisers.usage`: Each draws THE DJ's house set live in settled lights, and each is tested against a test tone so its mapping from sound to picture is known.
- `wtf.term.vote.meaning`: How an SDM read decides each bit: the activated hard locations add their counters and the sign wins.
- `wtf.term.vote.usage`: A read-address near a stored word activates many of the hard locations that word was written to, so their counters outvote the other words stored there. SDM EXPLORE shows the vote step by step.
- `wtf.term.vu-meters.meaning`: Two needles: the left reads the sound below 500 Hz, the right the sound above it.
- `wtf.term.vu-meters.usage`: One of the hero's eight visualisers, drawn from THE DJ's sound and shown in the slot the VISUALISERS bag holds.
- `wtf.term.wake.meaning`: How a pulls read chooses which hard locations activate: fixed, by density, or the top ones.
- `wtf.term.wake.usage`: Only with `via: :pulls`.
- `wtf.term.walker.meaning`: One copy of the numbers moving under the drift, or one trained model in a set; a cloud is many walkers.
- `wtf.term.walker.usage`: NUMBERS drifts walkers through the springs; GRADSETTLE ran four walkers at T 0.03 and read a doubt from their spread.
- `wtf.term.weirdlittlesdmguy.meaning`: A small SDM language model with one obsession, how we know things, and his tiny paper on one title page.
- `wtf.term.weirdlittlesdmguy.usage`: He wears his own mark in the menu, a little pixel robot in colour. His live chat runs in a dev build. The old addresses #/sdmguy and #/wlg redirect here.
- `wtf.term.what-chains.meaning`: Small shimmering words on the WHAT page that open in place into a short chain of lines, each chain in one neon.
- `wtf.term.what-chains.usage`: Nine chains, every path ends. what? sits beside the MCP line, the others in the opening paragraphs and the sections; the last, THE FINAL BOSS, asks no way. and answers. The home hero carries one what? that points at the first chain.
- `wtf.term.winamp-bars.meaning`: The house set as chunky bars, low notes left, each with a cap that hangs and falls.
- `wtf.term.winamp-bars.usage`: One of the hero's eight visualisers, drawn from THE DJ's sound and shown in the slot the VISUALISERS bag holds.
- `wtf.term.winamp-scope.meaning`: The sound wave as a row of dots, as an oscilloscope draws it.
- `wtf.term.winamp-scope.usage`: One of the hero's eight visualisers, drawn from THE DJ's sound and shown in the slot the VISUALISERS bag holds.
- `wtf.term.word-size.meaning`: The number of bits in an address and in a data word; SETTLE uses one length for both.
- `wtf.term.word-size.usage`: Kanerva: "The capacity of a location is referred to as the memory's word size, U." The keyword was `size:` on sdm, sdmscale, softsdm, contenttrack and refusal; the Hopfield `memory` statement keeps `size:` because it is not Kanerva's memory.
- `wtf.term.write-address.meaning`: The address a data word is stored at.
- `wtf.term.write-address.usage`: Flynn, Kanerva and Bhadkamkar: "a word can be read back not only by giving the original write address but also by giving one close to it." In SETTLE, `m.write :cat` names it: the pattern that belongs to :cat.
- `wtf.term.write-samples.meaning`: How many activated tries each soft write samples per hard location.
- `wtf.term.write-samples.usage`: 0 uses the exact probability instead.
- `wtf.term.write.meaning`: Writes a data word into a memory at its write-address: each activated hard location adds it to its bit-counters.
- `wtf.term.write.usage`: Written `m.write :cat`. The write-address is the pattern that belongs to :cat.
- `wtf.term.xor-bind.meaning`: The bind of Kanerva's hyperdimensional computing: c = a XOR b, bit by bit. Tying again with b gives back a, so a tie can be undone.
- `wtf.term.xor-bind.usage`: The KANERVA page ties each role to its value with XOR to work out the dollar of Mexico and Kanerva's other examples; a role tied to itself cancels to all zeros.
- `wtf.term.yayoi-kusama.meaning`: The artist of the infinity mirrored room that the site's brand picture comes from.
- `wtf.term.yayoi-kusama.usage`: CREDITS shows the brand picture as her work, for credit only. The footer's depth is inspired by her infinity mirror rooms.
- `wtf.top.cap`: $ glossary --search
- `wtf.top.docs`: the SETTLE docs
- `wtf.top.hint`: every term has its own link
- `wtf.top.search`: search the terms
- `wtf.top.sub`: The site's own dictionary, one record for every word.

## wya

- `wya.carry.kicker`: guide
- `wya.carry.label`: Switch guide
- `wya.chip.mcp`: served by settle-mcp
- `wya.chip.three`: 3 guides
- `wya.door.open`: open this guide
- `wya.door.programmer`: SETTLE alone, KANERVA alone, and the two together, for machine learning and for other problems. Real programs with their real output, then how to get started and where the detailed docs are.
- `wya.door.reading`: reading below
- `wya.door.sound`: A sound that follows the physics: heat becomes hiss, flips become crackle, the energy a falling drone. How to use it in a piece, one real example, then how to get started.
- `wya.door.visual`: A picture made of coins that comes out of noise, holds, breaks up when heated and forms again. How to use it in a piece, one real picture with its real numbers, then how to get started.
- `wya.doors.hint`: Press a door and its guide opens here.
- `wya.guides.label`: THREE GUIDES · ONE PER READER
- `wya.guides.title`: Pick your door
- `wya.h1`: Who you are
- `wya.intro`: SETTLE, KANERVA and settle-mcp are three things, and what they are for depends on who is asking. A programmer gets a sampler, a memory and a server. A visual artist gets a picture made of coins. A sound artist gets a sound that follows the physics.
- `wya.intro2.body`: Each guide says what this is in your terms, how to use it in your project (SETTLE alone, the memory alone, the two together), shows one real example with its real output, gets you started, and links into the detailed docs.
- `wya.intro2.mcp`: The same three guides are the first thing the MCP server hands an assistant.
- `wya.jump.label`: The three guides
- `wya.note`: The three guides are Markdown files in docs/who-you-are/, written in English and rendered here by the same renderer as the package docs. A reader in another language sees a translation only while it is current for the English, and the English otherwise. settle-mcp carries the same three files as resources and names them first in its AGENTS.md.
